## File: docs/sih_26027_architecture_and_regulatory_whitepaper.md
````markdown
  1: # IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI): Architecture & Regulatory Whitepaper
  2: **AI-Powered Automatic Block Planning and Corridor Optimization System for Indian Railways**  
  3: **Smart India Hackathon (SIH) Problem Statement 26027**
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: Indian Railways (IR) operates over 13,000 passenger trains and 8,000 freight trains daily across a 68,000 km route network. Maintaining track geometry, overhead equipment (OHE), and signaling infrastructure requires scheduled track possessions known as **maintenance blocks**. Currently, block planning across Indian Railways is largely decentralized, manual, and siloed within individual railway divisions.
 10: 
 11: Each engineering department—Civil (TMS), Electrical TRD (TDMS), and Signaling & Telecom (SMMS)—requests separate blocks through legacy portals or ad-hoc paperwork. Section Controllers manually reconcile these requests against live train paths using the Control Office Application (COA). This manual workflow creates three critical systemic failure modes:
 12: 
 13: 1. **Corridor Fragmentation:** Independent blocks on adjacent sections compound train delays rather than aligning downtime.
 14: 2. **Sub-Optimal Asset Utilization:** Track maintenance machines (e.g., Duomatic tampers, ballast cleaners) idle between isolated possessions.
 15: 3. **Safety Disconnect:** Temporary Speed Restrictions (TSRs) generated by maintenance activities require manual caution order issuance, creating potential failure points in driver compliance.
 16: 
 17: **IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI)** solves these structural bottlenecks by introducing an automated, multi-department optimization engine. Auto-BDMS pools maintenance defects from TMS, TDMS, and SMMS, evaluates corridor availability in COA, and executes a **Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP)** model to generate coordinated **Joint Shadow Blocks**. Furthermore, it integrates with **RDSO Kavach TCAS** (`RDSO/SPN/196/2020`) to electronically transmit Temporary Speed Restrictions directly to locomotive cabs.
 18: 
 19: ---
 20: 
 21: ## 1. Domain Systems & Data Ingestion Architecture
 22: 
 23: Auto-BDMS unifies four core Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS) data pipelines:
 24: 
 25: ```
 26: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 27: │                          CRIS DATA ECOSYSTEM                             │
 28: ├───────────────────┬───────────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────┤
 29: │    Civil Track    │  Electrical TRD   │ Signal & Telecom │ Live Traffic  │
 30: │       (TMS)       │      (TDMS)       │      (SMMS)      │     (COA)     │
 31: └─────────┬─────────┴─────────┬─────────┴────────┬─────────┴───────┬───────┘
 32:           │                   │                  │                 │
 33:           ▼                   ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 34: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 35: │                   IRIS AI UNIFIED INGESTION LAYER                   │
 36: │        (Geospatial Alignment, Chainage Normalization, Block Sizing)       │
 37: └─────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
 38:                                       │
 39:                                       ▼
 40: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 41: │              MULTI-DEPARTMENT SHADOW-BLOCK OPTIMIZER (MILP)              │
 42: └─────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
 43:                                       │
 44:           ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
 45:           ▼                                                       ▼
 46: ┌──────────────────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
 47: │    CONTROLLER DECISION COCKPIT   │            │        RDSO KAVACH TCAS          │
 48: │   (One-Click Sanctioning & COA)  │            │  (Direct Electronic TSR Stream)  │
 49: └──────────────────────────────────┘            └──────────────────────────────────┘
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ### 1.1 Source System Specifications
 53: 
 54: | Directorate | Legacy CRIS System | Ingested Data Attributes | Urgency Metrics |
 55: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 56: | **Civil Engineering** | **TMS** (Track Management System) | Track Geometry Index (TGI), USFD weld defects, sleeper replacement backlog, deep screening requisitions | P1: Rail fracture, weld flaw > 8mm; P2: TGI < 36; P3: Cyclical tamping |
 57: | **Electrical TRD** | **TDMS** (Traction Distribution Mgmt System) | OHE contact wire wear, isolator testing, insulator washing, tensioning checks | P1: Contact wire thickness < 8.25mm; P2: Stagger deviation; P3: Tree trimming |
 58: | **Signaling & Telecom** | **SMMS** (Signal Maintenance Mgmt System) | Point machine health, axle counter calibration, track circuit relay testing | P1: Point detection failure; P2: Relay timing drift; P3: Cable insulation check |
 59: | **Operating (Traffic)** | **COA** (Control Office Application) | Live train GPS, timetables, section headways, freight rake paths, loop capacities | Passenger train priority rankings (Rajdhani/Vande Bharat > Mail/Express > Freight) |
 60: 
 61: ---
 62: 
 63: ## 2. Multi-Department Joint Shadow Blocking
 64: 
 65: ### 2.1 The Shadow Block Concept
 66: In traditional operations, if the Civil Department secures a 3-hour block on Track Section A, the Electrical and Signaling departments may not be notified in time to mobilize. Days later, Electrical takes another 2.5-hour block on the exact same line.
 67: 
 68: **Shadow Blocking** identifies the primary constraint (e.g., a major 4-hour track relaying possession) and dynamically schedules secondary and tertiary maintenance tasks from other directorates within the spatial and temporal shadow of the primary block.
 69: 
 70: ```
 71: TRADITIONAL SILOED MODEL:
 72: Day 1: [--- Civil Tamping: 3.5 hrs ---] (Electrical & Signal idle)
 73: Day 3:                                    [--- OHE Inspection: 2.5 hrs ---] (Civil idle)
 74: Day 5:                                                                       [--- Signal Overhaul: 2.0 hrs ---]
 75: Total Corridor Disruption: 8.0 Hours
 76: 
 77: IRIS AI JOINT SHADOW-BLOCK MODEL:
 78: Day 1: ┌─── PRIMARY: Civil Track Relay (4.0 hrs) ──────────────────────────┐
 79:        ├─── SHADOW 1: Electrical OHE Wire Adjustment (3.0 hrs concurrent) ──┤
 80:        └─── SHADOW 2: S&T Point Machine Lubrication (1.5 hrs concurrent) ───┘
 81: Total Corridor Disruption: 4.0 Hours (50% Reduction in Lost Line Capacity)
 82: ```
 83: 
 84: ---
 85: 
 86: ## 3. Mathematical Optimization Formulation (MILP)
 87: 
 88: Auto-BDMS solves block scheduling as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) using Google OR-Tools:
 89: 
 90: ### 3.1 Objective Function
 91: $$\min Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in B} \text{TrainDelayCost}(i) + \beta \sum_{j \in D} \text{PendingRiskPenalty}(j) - \gamma \sum_{k \in S} \text{ShadowBlockSynergy}(k)$$
 92: 
 93: Where:
 94: * $B$ is the set of scheduled maintenance blocks.
 95: * $D$ is the set of unserved infrastructure defects across TMS, TDMS, and SMMS.
 96: * $S$ is the set of co-located joint blocks bundled together.
 97: * $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are operational weights tuned for network congestion:
 98:   * $\alpha = 0.45$: Cost of passenger and freight delay minutes.
 99:   * $\beta = 0.40$: Safety risk factor for deferred P1/P2 maintenance.
100:   * $\gamma = 0.15$: Multi-department coordination reward.
101: 
102: ### 3.2 Hard Operational Constraints
103: 
104: 1. **Headway & Corridor Window:**
105:    $$\text{BlockStartTime}(b) \ge \text{PassageTime}(\text{PrecedingTrain}) + T_{\text{safety\_headway}}$$
106: 2. **Machine & Crew Contiguity:**
107:    A track tamper or OHE tower wagon cannot be assigned to two distant stations without transit time:
108:    $$\text{StartTime}(b_{m, 2}) \ge \text{EndTime}(b_{m, 1}) + \text{TransitTime}(\text{Loc}_1, \text{Loc}_2)$$
109: 3. **Safety Interlocking Lockout:**
110:    $$\text{TrackCircuitStatus}(\text{Section}_k) = \text{OCCUPIED} \implies \text{SignalAspect}(\text{EntrySignal}) = \text{RED}$$
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## 4. Multi-Horizon Planning Framework
115: 
116: Auto-BDMS divides corridor planning into three distinct operational horizons:
117: 
118: ```
119: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
120: │                         MULTI-HORIZON TIMELINE MATRIX                          │
121: ├──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┤
122: │    24-HOUR TACTICAL      │    7-DAY OPERATIONAL     │    30-DAY STRATEGIC      │
123: │  (Real-Time Disruption)  │    (Weekly Rolling)      │   (Master Corridor)      │
124: ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
125: │ • Night Lull (00:00-04:00)│ • Coordinated Mega-Blocks│ • TGI Degradation Curves │
126: │ • P1 Emergency Fixes     │ • Inter-division machine │ • Rail Renewal Programs  │
127: │ • Live COA Headway Fit   │   sharing & logistics    │ • Machine Overhaul Cycles│
128: │ • Instant Kavach TSR Push│ • Passenger Diversions   │ • Long-term budget opt.  │
129: └──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
130: ```
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ## 5. RDSO Regulatory & Kavach TCAS Compliance
135: 
136: ### 5.1 Regulatory Framework
137: Auto-BDMS strictly complies with Indian Railways statutory manuals and specifications:
138: 
139: 1. **Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual (IRPWM - 2020 Edition):**
140:    * Regulates permissible track geometry tolerances, USFD flaw classification, and mandatory speed reductions post-maintenance.
141: 2. **AC Traction Manual (ACTM - Volume II):**
142:    * Prescribes OHE power block protocols and electrical earthing clearances.
143: 3. **Indian Railways Signal Engineering Manual (IRSEM - 2021 Edition):**
144:    * Dictates interlock testing requirements and axle counter isolation procedures.
145: 4. **RDSO Kavach TCAS Specification (`RDSO/SPN/196/2020`):**
146:    * Defines direct wireless communication between trackside Radio Block Centers (RBC), Stationary Kavach, and Onboard Locomotive Kavach units.
147: 
148: ### 5.2 Emergency Braking Distance (EBD) Physics
149: When maintenance requires a speed restriction (TSR), Auto-BDMS computes the exact deceleration envelope using the RDSO Kavach physical braking model:
150: 
151: $$D_{\text{stop}} = \frac{V^2}{2g(\mu + G)} + V \cdot t_{\text{reaction}}$$
152: 
153: Where:
154: * $V$ = Locomotive velocity ($\text{m/s}$)
155: * $g$ = Gravitational acceleration ($9.81\text{ m/s}^2$)
156: * $\mu$ = Dynamic track friction coefficient (Monsoon Wet: $0.095$, Fog: $0.115$, Dry: $0.134$)
157: * $G$ = Track gradient (e.g., $+0.002$ for rising gradient, $-0.003$ for falling)
158: * $t_{\text{reaction}}$ = Kavach brake system latency ($1.2\text{ s}$ autonomous, $2.5\text{ s}$ advisory)
159: 
160: ### 5.3 Explainable AI Audit Dossier (RDSO Form 14B)
161: To ensure compliance with Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) guidelines, every automated intervention is immutably logged across 4 chronological stages with an SHA-256 digital verification seal:
162: 
163: 1. **Stage 1 (Vision / Ingestion):** Hazard / Defect detection timestamp and raw telemetry.
164: 2. **Stage 2 (Kinematics / Headway):** Speed, distance to asset, and line availability.
165: 3. **Stage 3 (Physics / MILP Evaluation):** Stopping distance envelope and corridor cost balance.
166: 4. **Stage 4 (Actuation / Sanction):** Kavach solenoid trigger or Section Controller sanction.
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: ## 6. Target Impact & Performance Metrics
171: 
172: | Metric | Legacy Decentralized Planning | IRIS AI Auto-BDMS | Impact |
173: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
174: | **Corridor Downtime** | 6–8 hrs / week per 100km | 3.5–4.5 hrs / week per 100km | **35–45% Reduction** |
175: | **Machine Utilization** | 42% active operating hours | 68% active operating hours | **+26% Asset Productivity** |
176: | **Planning Latency** | 2–3 days manual coordination | < 30 seconds MILP solver | **Near Real-Time** |
177: | **TSR Compliance** | Manual paper caution orders | 100% Direct Kavach TCAS injection | **Zero Human Error Risk** |
178: | **Punctuality Impact** | 12–18 mins delay per block | 4–6 mins average delay | **~65% Delay Reduction** |
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ## Conclusion
183: 
184: IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI) transforms railway maintenance from a fragmented, reactive chore into a synchronized, mathematically optimized corridor strategy. By bridging Civil, Electrical, and Signal engineering silos with live traffic controllers and direct Kavach safety automation, Auto-BDMS delivers maximum asset availability while upholding the highest standards of railway safety.
````

## File: src/app/api/keepalive/route.ts
````typescript
 1: // src/app/api/keepalive/route.ts
 2: // Automated Keep-Alive Pinger to prevent Render free instance from sleeping
 3: import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
 4: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';
 5: export async function GET() {
 6:   const targetUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
 7:     ? `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/system/status`
 8:     : 'https://railsuraksha-ai.onrender.com/api/v1/system/status';
 9:   try {
10:     const startTime = Date.now();
11:     const res = await fetch(targetUrl, {
12:       cache: 'no-store',
13:       headers: {
14:         'User-Agent': 'RailSuraksha-KeepAlive-Worker/1.0',
15:       },
16:     });
17:     const elapsed = Date.now() - startTime;
18:     return NextResponse.json({
19:       status: 'ok',
20:       targetUrl,
21:       httpStatus: res.status,
22:       latencyMs: elapsed,
23:       timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
24:     });
25:   } catch (error: unknown) {
26:     return NextResponse.json(
27:       {
28:         status: 'error',
29:         targetUrl,
30:         message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
31:         timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
32:       },
33:       { status: 500 }
34:     );
35:   }
36: }
````

## File: src/lib/agents/kavachBrakingAgent.ts
````typescript
 1: import { EbdCalculationResult, WeatherCondition } from '@/types/apiContracts';
 2: export interface BrakingInputs {
 3:   trainId: string;
 4:   velocityKmh: number;
 5:   obstacleDistanceMeters: number;
 6:   frictionCoefficient?: number; // default steel rail mu = 0.134
 7:   gradientPercent?: number;     // default G = 0.002
 8:   reactionTimeSeconds?: number;// default t_reaction = 2.0s
 9:   weatherCondition?: WeatherCondition;
10: }
11: /**
12:  * Returns RDSO-standard adjusted friction coefficient and reaction buffer based on atmospheric conditions
13:  */
14: export function getWeatherFrictionParams(weather: WeatherCondition): {
15:   frictionCoefficient: number;
16:   reactionTimeMultiplier: number;
17:   label: string;
18:   riskFactor: string;
19: } {
20:   switch (weather) {
21:     case 'WET_MONSOON':
22:       return {
23:         frictionCoefficient: 0.095, // Hydroplaning risk on wet steel rail
24:         reactionTimeMultiplier: 1.25,
25:         label: 'Monsoon Heavy Rain',
26:         riskFactor: 'HIGH SLIPPAGE (+35% Stopping Distance)',
27:       };
28:     case 'DENSE_FOG':
29:       return {
30:         frictionCoefficient: 0.115, // Dew/moisture on cold rail
31:         reactionTimeMultiplier: 1.4,
32:         label: 'Severe Winter Fog',
33:         riskFactor: 'LIMITED SIGHT DISTANCE (220m HUD Cap)',
34:       };
35:     case 'NIGHT_IR':
36:       return {
37:         frictionCoefficient: 0.130,
38:         reactionTimeMultiplier: 1.1,
39:         label: 'Night Vision IR',
40:         riskFactor: 'THERMAL SPECTRAL ENHANCED',
41:       };
42:     case 'DRY':
43:     default:
44:       return {
45:         frictionCoefficient: 0.134,
46:         reactionTimeMultiplier: 1.0,
47:         label: 'Clear Dry Track',
48:         riskFactor: 'OPTIMAL ADHESION',
49:       };
50:   }
51: }
52: /**
53:  * Calculates RDSO Emergency Braking Distance (EBD):
54:  * D_stop = (V^2 / (2 * g * (mu + G))) + (V * t_reaction)
55:  */
56: export function calculateKavachEbd(inputs: BrakingInputs): EbdCalculationResult {
57:   const weatherParams = inputs.weatherCondition ? getWeatherFrictionParams(inputs.weatherCondition) : null;
58:   const effectiveFriction = weatherParams ? weatherParams.frictionCoefficient : (inputs.frictionCoefficient ?? 0.134);
59:   const effectiveReactionTime = weatherParams ? (1.96 * weatherParams.reactionTimeMultiplier) : (inputs.reactionTimeSeconds ?? 1.96);
60:   const {
61:     trainId,
62:     velocityKmh,
63:     obstacleDistanceMeters,
64:     gradientPercent = 0.002,
65:   } = inputs;
66:   const frictionCoefficient = effectiveFriction;
67:   const reactionTimeSeconds = effectiveReactionTime;
68:   const g = 9.81; // Acceleration due to gravity (m/s^2)
69:   const vMs = (velocityKmh * 1000) / 3600; // Convert km/h to m/s
70:   // Braking distance component
71:   const dBrake = Math.pow(vMs, 2) / (2 * g * (frictionCoefficient + gradientPercent));
72:   // Reaction distance component
73:   const dReaction = vMs * reactionTimeSeconds;
74:   // Total calculated stopping distance
75:   const calculatedStoppingDistanceMeters = Math.round(dBrake + dReaction);
76:   const marginDistanceMeters = obstacleDistanceMeters - calculatedStoppingDistanceMeters;
77:   const isCollisionRisk = calculatedStoppingDistanceMeters >= obstacleDistanceMeters;
78:   return {
79:     trainId,
80:     velocityKmh,
81:     obstacleDistanceMeters,
82:     calculatedStoppingDistanceMeters,
83:     marginDistanceMeters,
84:     isCollisionRisk,
85:     requiredDecelerationMs2: Number((Math.pow(vMs, 2) / (2 * obstacleDistanceMeters)).toFixed(2)),
86:     brakeState: isCollisionRisk ? 'EMERGENCY_SOLENOID_ACTUATED' : 'CLEAR'
87:   };
88: }
````

## File: generate_writeup_pdf.py
````python
  1: """
  2: IRIS AI - Markdown to Publication-Grade PDF Generator
  3: Reads 'docs/MASTER_RESEARCH_AND_SYSTEM_WRITEUP.md' and compiles a beautifully styled,
  4: high-density executive PDF document with custom running headers/footers, Mermaid code boxes,
  5: formatted tables, and Light-Blue Mintlify visual styling.
  6: """
  7: import os
  8: import sys
  9: import re
 10: from reportlab.lib import colors
 11: from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
 12: from reportlab.lib.units import inch
 13: from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet, ParagraphStyle
 14: from reportlab.platypus import (
 15:     SimpleDocTemplate,
 16:     Paragraph,
 17:     Spacer,
 18:     Table,
 19:     TableStyle,
 20:     PageBreak,
 21:     KeepTogether,
 22:     HRFlowable,
 23:     Preformatted
 24: )
 25: from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
 26: class NumberedCanvas(canvas.Canvas):
 27:     """
 28:     Two-pass canvas to dynamically compute and render total page numbers
 29:     along with professional running headers and footers.
 30:     """
 31:     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
 32:         super(NumberedCanvas, self).__init__(*args, **kwargs)
 33:         self._saved_page_states = []
 34:     def showPage(self):
 35:         self._saved_page_states.append(dict(self.__dict__))
 36:         self._startPage()
 37:     def save(self):
 38:         num_pages = len(self._saved_page_states)
 39:         for state in self._saved_page_states:
 40:             self.__dict__.update(state)
 41:             self.draw_page_decorations(num_pages)
 42:             super(NumberedCanvas, self).showPage()
 43:         super(NumberedCanvas, self).save()
 44:     def draw_page_decorations(self, page_count):
 45:         if self._pageNumber == 1:
 46:             # Skip header on cover page
 47:             return
 48:         self.saveState()
 49:         self.setFont("Helvetica-Bold", 8)
 50:         self.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#1E3A8A"))
 51:         # Running Header
 52:         self.drawString(54, 750, "IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI)")
 53:         self.setFont("Helvetica", 8)
 54:         self.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#64748B"))
 55:         self.drawString(195, 750, "|  SIH 26027 Master Research & System Architecture Dossier")
 56:         self.setStrokeColor(colors.HexColor("#CBD5E1"))
 57:         self.setLineWidth(0.5)
 58:         self.line(54, 742, 558, 742)
 59:         # Running Footer
 60:         self.line(54, 48, 558, 48)
 61:         self.drawString(54, 36, "Confidential & Statutory - Ministry of Railways (CRIS & RDSO Standards)")
 62:         page_text = f"Page {self._pageNumber} of {page_count}"
 63:         self.drawRightString(558, 36, page_text)
 64:         self.restoreState()
 65: def clean_markdown_inline(text):
 66:     """Converts standard markdown inline tags to ReportLab Paragraph HTML tags."""
 67:     # Convert bold-italic ***text*** or ___text___
 68:     text = re.sub(r'\*\*\*(.*?)\*\*\*', r'<b><i>\1</i></b>', text)
 69:     # Convert bold **text**
 70:     text = re.sub(r'\*\*(.*?)\*\*', r'<b>\1</b>', text)
 71:     # Convert italic *text* or _text_
 72:     text = re.sub(r'\*(.*?)\*', r'<i>\1</i>', text)
 73:     text = re.sub(r'_(.*?)_', r'<i>\1</i>', text)
 74:     # Convert inline code `code`
 75:     text = re.sub(r'`(.*?)`', r'<font face="Courier" color="#1E3A8A"><b>\1</b></font>', text)
 76:     # Clean latex math $...$
 77:     text = re.sub(r'\$(.*?)\$', r'<i>\1</i>', text)

 86: 
 87: ## 🛤️ 4. Detailed End-to-End Operational Journeys
 88: 
 89: ---
 90: 
 91: ### Journey 1: Automated Multi-Department Bundling & Sanction (Happy Path)
 92: 
 93: * **Primary Persona:** Divisional Section Controller (`Sr. DOM`), Department Planners (Civil, Electrical, S&T).
 94: * **Preconditions:** Daily sync from CRIS databases (TMS, TDMS, SMMS, COA) completed for CSMT–Kalyan corridor.
 95: 
 96: #### Step-by-Step Flow:
 97: 1. **Multi-Source Requisition Ingestion:**
 98:    * Civil Engineering registers a track tamping demand on Section `KM 108/4 to 112/2` (TMS).
 99:    * Electrical TRD registers a 25kV OHE catenary replacement demand on `KM 109/1 to 114/6` (TDMS).
100:    * S&T registers point machine `SW-04` stroke calibration on `KM 110/2 to 111/0` (SMMS).
101: 2. **Spatial Chainage Normalization:**
102:    * The Unified Ingestion Adapter maps all three continuous linear chainages to logical track circuit **`TC-03`** (Dadar Section).
103: 3. **ML Urgency Triage:**
104:    * Dynamic scoring categorizes demands as `P1_CRITICAL` (flaw score 0.94), `P2_SCHEDULED` (wear score 0.78), and `P2_SCHEDULED` (stroke score 0.72).
105: 4. **CP-SAT Corridor Optimization:**
106:    * Google OR-Tools CP-SAT analyzes the COA train timetable and identifies an off-peak nocturnal white corridor between **01:30 IST and 04:45 IST** (195 minutes).
107:    * Bundles all three demands into a single **Joint Shadow Block (`BLK-JOINT-0906-01`)**.
108:    * Computes **85 minutes of saved downtime (38.4% reduction)** compared to 3 isolated blocks.
109: 5. **Controller Review & Sanction:**
110:    * Section Controller views the proposed shaded rectangular block zone on the **Corridor Time-Distance String Chart**.
111:    * Clicks `[APPROVE & SANCTION BLOCK]`.
112: 6. **Safety Dissemination & Lockout:**
113:    * Kavach TCAS broadcasts a digital $30\text{ km/h}$ Temporary Speed Restriction (TSR) to approaching train cabs.
114:    * Station Master interlocking console locks signal `S-12` to danger (`RED`) per **Form S&T/T-351**.
115:    * Digital **Form T/409 Caution Order** is distributed to loco pilots.
116:    * Decision Dossier is signed with **SHA-256 hash** and archived for RDSO Form 14B compliance.
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ### Journey 2: Emergency P1 USFD Rail Defect Interruption (Tactical Exception)
121: 
122: * **Primary Persona:** Section Controller, Locomotive Pilot, P-Way SSE.
123: * **Preconditions:** Normal daytime traffic running on Up Fast line.
124: 
125: #### Step-by-Step Flow:
126: 1. **Defect Detection:**
127:    * Ultrasonic Flaw Detection (USFD) car identifies an **IMR** (*Immediate Removal*) transverse rail fracture on `TC-03` (`KM 108/6`).
128: 2. **Instant Emergency Triage:**
129:    * ML Urgency Triage immediately flags the defect as **P1 Critical (Score 0.98)**.
130: 3. **Automated Safety Protection:**
131:    * IRIS AI immediately triggers an emergency Kavach TSR broadcast capping section speed to **$15\text{ km/h}$** per *IRPWM 2020*.
132:    * Approaching Locomotive Cab displays 1200Hz audible warning tone and overlays the safe deceleration braking curve.
133: 4. **Dynamic Rescheduling:**
134:    * The CP-SAT solver automatically adjusts the tactical 24h schedule, routing freight rakes to loop sidings and allocating an emergency 60-minute clamping window in the nearest 45-minute traffic gap.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ### Journey 3: Controller Block Rejection & Real-Time Re-Optimization
139: 
140: * **Primary Persona:** Divisional Section Controller.
141: * **Preconditions:** AI proposes a 02:00 AM joint block on Section B.
142: 
143: #### Step-by-Step Flow:
144: 1. **Operational Conflict Identified:**
145:    * Controller notes that Premium Express Train #12138 is running 35 minutes behind schedule due to upstream weather delays.
146: 2. **Controller Rejection:**
147:    * Controller clicks `[REJECT PROPOSED BLOCK]`.
148:    * Enters rejection reason: *"Express 12138 delayed; cannot clear section before 02:15 AM"*.
149:    * Sets preferred search constraint: *"Window after 02:45 AM"*.
150: 3. **Automated Re-Optimization:**
151:    * The CP-SAT solver re-computes the corridor model in **$< 15\text{ seconds}$**.
152:    * Produces an adjusted 02:50 AM to 05:00 AM joint block window, preserving zero passenger delay while maintaining 100% of planned maintenance tasks.
153: 4. **Sanction:** Controller approves the updated plan.
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ### Journey 4: Safety & Regulatory Compliance Audit Review
158: 
159: * **Primary Persona:** Safety Compliance Auditor / RDSO Inspector.
160: * **Preconditions:** Previous night's block operations completed.
161: 
162: #### Step-by-Step Flow:
163: 1. **Auditor Log Access:**
164:    * RDSO Inspector logs into the **Auditor Workspace** and queries Block ID `BLK-JOINT-0906-01`.
165: 2. **4-Step Explainable Audit Inspection:**
166:    * *Step 1 (Ingestion):* Verifies raw TMS flaw ticket, TDMS catenary log, and SMMS point notice.
167:    * *Step 2 (Conflict Check):* Verifies 15-minute passenger train clearance headway ($\Delta_{\text{clear}}$).
168:    * *Step 3 (Shadow Bundling):* Verifies that double-discharge earthing buffers ($\Delta_{\text{earth}} \ge 10\text{m}$) were scheduled.
169:    * *Step 4 (Safety Actuation):* Verifies that Kavach TSR 30 km/h was acknowledged by approaching train OBUs.
170: 3. **Cryptographic Validation & Export:**
171:    * System verifies the SHA-256 digital seal matches the original timestamped record.
172:    * Auditor clicks `[EXPORT RDSO FORM 14B]`, generating an official signed compliance certificate.
````

## File: docs/06_techspec.md
````markdown
 1: # IRIS AI — Technical Specification & Non-Functional Requirements
 2: 
 3: **System Name:** IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI): Automatic Block Planning & Corridor Optimization  
 4: **Problem Statement:** SIH 26027 — *"AI-Powered Automatic Block Planning to Maximize Asset Availability for Train Operations on Indian Railways"*  
 5: **Document Version:** 3.1.0 (Grounded Multi-Horizon & Decoupled Architecture Specification)  
 6: **Governing Standards Reference:** IRPWM 2020, ACTM Vol II, IRSEM 2021, G&SR Chapter 15, RDSO/SPN/196/2020 Kavach Ver 4.0.
 7: 
 8: ---
 9: 
10: ## 💻 1. Core Technology Stack & Architectural Patterns
11: 
12: ```text
13: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
14: │                                   TECHNOLOGY STACK MATRIX                              │
15: ├────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┤
16: │ LAYER                      │ PRIMARY TECHNOLOGY         │ KEY LIBRARIES & FRAMEWORKS   │
17: ├────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
18: │ Architecture Style         │ Hexagonal Ports & Adapters │ Pluggable Ingestion/Actuation│
19: │ Frontend Web App           │ Next.js 16 (App Router)    │ React 19, TypeScript 5+      │
20: │ Styling & Tokens           │ Tailwind CSS v4            │ Vanilla CSS, Mintlify Theme  │
21: │ Charting & Data Visualizer │ Recharts + High-Perf SVG   │ recharts, Lucide, Framer Mot.│
22: │ Backend API Services       │ FastAPI (Python 3.12) / TS │ Pydantic v2, Uvicorn, SSE    │
23: │ Mathematical Solver        │ Google OR-Tools CP-SAT     │ ortools.sat.python.cp_model  │
24: │ Policy & Config Engine     │ Externalized Config/JSONB  │ Pydantic Settings, Redis 7   │
25: │ Graph Topology             │ NetworkX 3.2+              │ Track Circuit Adjacency DAG  │
26: │ Audio Synthesizer          │ Pure Web Audio API         │ 800Hz / 1200Hz RDSO Chimes   │
27: │ Persistence & Cache        │ PostgreSQL 16 / Redis 7    │ Prisma ORM / pgvector        │
28: └────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
29: ```
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 🔌 2. Decoupled Architecture & Pluggability Engine
34: 
35: ### 2.1 Pluggable Ingestion Interface (`IIngestionAdapter`)
36: All external data feeds are ingested through strongly-typed abstraction interfaces:
37: ```typescript
38: export interface IIngestionAdapter<TRawPayload, TNormalizedEntity> {
39:   readonly adapterName: string;
40:   readonly schemaVersion: string;
41:   validate(raw: TRawPayload): Promise<boolean>;
42:   normalize(raw: TRawPayload, policy: DivisionalPolicyProfile): Promise<TNormalizedEntity[]>;
43: }
44: ```
45: * **Simulation Adapter:** Generates grounded synthetic corridor feeds (CSMT–Kalyan) for rapid local development and demo testing.
46: * **Configurable File/CSV Adapter:** Ingests ad-hoc division CSV/JSON export files with mapping profiles.
47: * **Enterprise CRIS Adapter:** Connects to live TMS, TDMS, SMMS, and COA REST/SOAP endpoints without altering core solver logic.
48: 
49: ### 2.2 Externalized Policy & Constraint Engine (`PolicyConfigService`)
50: * **No Hardcoded Domain Rules:** All safety headways ($\Delta_{\text{clear}}$), earthing buffers ($\Delta_{\text{earth}}, \Delta_{\text{restore}}$), urgency weight factors ($w_s, w_d, w_c$), and speed caps ($V_{\text{TSR}}$) are injected via `DivisionalPolicyProfile`.
51: * **Runtime Calibration:** Division controllers can adjust safety buffers per division or weather season without code re-deployment.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## ⚡ 3. Non-Functional Requirements & Performance SLAs
56: 
57: ### 3.1 Optimization Engine Performance SLAs `[Grounded Core]`
58: * **Multi-Horizon Solve Latency:**
59:   * **24-Hour Tactical Horizon:** Returns verified optimal or near-optimal ($< 2\%\text{ gap}$) block plan in **$< 30\text{ seconds}$** for a 100km corridor.
60:   * **7-Day Operational Horizon:** Solves weekly rolling corridor maintenance in **$< 90\text{ seconds}$**.
61:   * **30-Day Strategic Horizon:** Solves monthly cyclical maintenance in **$< 180\text{ seconds}$**.
62: * **Emergency Flaw Re-Optimization:** Upon sudden P1 rail defect insertion, solver re-routing must complete in **$< 15\text{ seconds}$**.
63: * **Solver Determinism & Feasibility:** Incorporates continuous soft slack penalties ($q_i = \max(0, c_i - \tau_i^S)$) ensuring it never crashes or returns an empty/infeasible result under extreme network degradation.
64: 
65: ### 3.2 Frontend Responsiveness & Rendering Performance
66: * **Recharts Client Rendering & SSR Isolation:** All charting components utilize `'use client'` boundaries and client-only dynamic loading (`next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`) to avoid SVG hydration mismatch between server and client.
67: * **SVG String Chart Smoothness:** Must maintain **60 fps** hardware-accelerated rendering during time-scrubbing, zooming, and panning.
68: * **Zero Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS):** Dynamic train path line rendering and Recharts `ResponsiveContainer` wrapping must not cause layout jumping ($\text{CLS} < 0.05$).
69: * **First Contentful Paint (FCP):** $\text{FCP} < 1.2\text{ seconds}$ on standard railway division broadband networks.
70: 
71: ### 3.3 Real-Time Safety & Actuation Latencies
72: * **Kavach TSR Broadcast Packet Generation:** $\le 200\text{ ms}$ from Section Controller click to wireless packet emission.
73: * **Electronic Interlocking Clamping:** Relay lockout status updated across all connected client interfaces in $\le 500\text{ ms}$ via WebSockets.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 🔒 4. Security, Integrity & Compliance Architecture
78: 
79: ### 4.1 Cryptographic Audit Trail (RDSO Form 14B)
80: * Every sanctioned block plan produces an immutable 4-step explainable record sealed with a **`SHA-256`** hash:
81:   $$\text{AuditSeal} = \text{SHA256}(\text{BlockId} + \text{OperatorId} + \text{Timestamp} + \text{BundledDemands} + \text{TSRSpeed} + \text{PolicyVersion})$$
82: * Tamper detection: Any modification to underlying work order times or policy profiles invalidates the cryptographic verification signature.
83: 
84: ### 4.2 Fail-Safe Architectural Defaults
85: * **Signal Aspect Clamping:** In the event of system network loss or database disconnection, all active maintenance block signals default to danger (`RED`) in fail-safe relay logic.
86: * **Kavach ATP Speed Supervision:** Onboard locomotive Kavach units enforce speed restrictions until explicit, verified digital clearance is received from the Radio Block Center (RBC).
87: 
88: ### 4.3 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
89: * Strict JWT session-based token authentication separating `SECTION_CONTROLLER` sanction rights from `DEPARTMENT_PLANNER` submission rights, `POLICY_ADMINISTRATOR` tuning rights, and `SAFETY_AUDITOR` inspection privileges.
````

## File: docs/14_design.md
````markdown
  1: # IRIS AI — Design System & Visual Style Guide (DESIGN.md)
  2: 
  3: **System Name:** IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI): Automatic Block Planning & Corridor Optimization  
  4: **Design Theme:** Light-Blue Mintlify Discipline  
  5: **Document Version:** 3.0.0 (Unified Grounded Specification)  
  6: **Governing Aesthetics:** Clean, authoritative, atmospheric light-blue canvas, crisp borders, precision data typography, zero AI-slop, strictly 4px button/input radius, strictly zero pill buttons.
  7: 
  8: ---
  9: 
 10: ## 🎨 1. Color Palette & Surface Tokens
 11: 
 12: ```text
 13: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 14: │                              MINTLIFY LIGHT-BLUE DESIGN SYSTEM                         │
 15: ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 16: │ SURFACE LEVELS:                                                                        │
 17: │ • Canvas Base (Surface 0):       #F0F6FC  (Soft ice-blue canvas)                       │
 18: │ • Card Surface (Surface 1):      #FFFFFF  (Pure white with #D0DFEE border)             │
 19: │ • Elevated Panel (Surface 2):    #E6F0FA  (Subtle cool tinted background)              │
 20: │ • Inset / Input Fill:            #F8FAFC  (Crisp subtle input fill)                    │
 21: ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 22: │ BRAND ACCENTS:                                                                         │
 23: │ • Signal Blue (Primary Brand):   #2B7FFF  (Vibrant, authoritative action accent)       │
 24: │ • Twilight Blue (Secondary):     #426188  (Atmospheric header & chart element accent)  │
 25: │ • Sky Blue (Hover / Focus Ring): #60A5FA  (Interactive focus state)                    │
 26: ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 27: │ TYPOGRAPHY & TEXT TOKENS:                                                              │
 28: │ • Ink Slate (Text Primary):      #0F172A  (Deep slate black for maximum readability)   │
 29: │ • Muted Slate (Text Secondary):  #475569  (Labels, subtitles, secondary metadata)     │
 30: │ • Faint Slate (Text Tertiary):   #94A3B8  (Grid lines, borders, placeholder text)      │
 31: ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 32: │ OPERATIONAL STATUS COLORS:                                                             │
 33: │ • P1 Critical / Hazard / Stop:   #EF4444  (Background: #FEE2E2, Border: #FCA5A5)       │
 34: │ • P2 Scheduled / Caution:        #F59E0B  (Background: #FEF3C7, Border: #FCD34D)       │
 35: │ • P3 Routine / Operational / Clr:#10B981  (Background: #DCFCE7, Border: #86EFAC)       │
 36: └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: ---
 40: 
 41: ## 📐 2. Geometry & Spatial Layout Rules
 42: 
 43: * **Button / Input Border Radius:** Strictly **`4px`** (crisp, professional engineering aesthetic).
 44: * **Card / Panel Border Radius:** **`16px`** with `1px solid #D0DFEE`.
 45: * **Container / Modal Border Radius:** **`24px`** with soft drop-shadow (`box-shadow: 0 10px 25px -5px rgba(43, 127, 255, 0.08)`).
 46: * **Strict Prohibition:** **STRICTLY ZERO PILL BUTTONS** (`rounded-full` is prohibited for buttons and interactive controls). Only compact numeric indicator dots and micro status pills are rounded.
 47: 
 48: ---
 49: 
 50: ## 🔤 3. Typography & Numerical Data Rules
 51: 
 52: * **Primary UI Font Family:** `Inter`, `-apple-system`, `BlinkMacSystemFont`, `sans-serif` (clean, accessible, high-legibility at small sizes).
 53: * **Tabular / Telemetry Font Family:** `JetBrains Mono`, `ui-monospace`, `SFMono-Regular`, `monospace`.
 54:   * **Mandatory Usage:** All railway linear chainages (`KM 108/4`), Track Circuit IDs (`TC-03`), Signal IDs (`S-12`), speed values (`30 km/h`), timestamps (`01:30:00 IST`), and SHA-256 cryptographic hashes must use the monospaced font with tabular figure alignment (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`).
 55: 
 56: ---
 57: 
 58: ## 📊 4. Time-Distance String Chart Aesthetics
 59: 
 60: * **Canvas Background:** `#FFFFFF` with `#F0F6FC` subtle horizontal grid banding representing station zones.
 61: * **Station Axis (Y-Axis):** Dark `#0F172A` text labels on the left with kilometer offsets in `JetBrains Mono`.
 62: * **Timeline Axis (X-Axis):** 24-hour horizontal scale with hourly tick marks and vertical guidelines (`#E2E8F0`).
 63: * **Train Trajectories:**
 64:   * Rajdhani / Vande Bharat (Premium): Solid Signal Blue line (`#2B7FFF`, `stroke-width: 2.5px`).
 65:   * Mail / Express (Standard): Purple line (`#8B5CF6`, `stroke-width: 2.0px`).
 66:   * Goods / Freight Rakes: Dashed Slate line (`#64748B`, `stroke-dasharray: 4 2`).
 67: * **Bundled Shadow Block Zone:**
 68:   * Shaded rectangular area with `#2B7FFF` fill at `12% opacity`.
 69:   * Border: `1.5px solid #2B7FFF`.
 70:   * Overlay: Diagonal cross-hatch pattern displaying savings badge (`⚡ 38.4% Downtime Saved`).
 71: 
 72: ---

 74: ## 🔊 5. Acoustic & Micro-Animation Tokens

 76: * **Audio Warning Synthesizer:** Pure Web Audio API generating authentic RDSO cab chimes:
 77:   * *1200 Hz Caution Tone:* 300ms duration sinusoidal beep for active TSR approach.

 85: ## 📈 6. Recharts Visual Theme & Chart Tokens

 90: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

100: ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

103: │ • Tooltip Box Shadow:           0 4px 12px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.08)                      │

109: * **Reference Lines:**

111:   * Amber dashed (`#F59E0B`, `strokeDasharray: "3 3"`, `strokeWidth: 2`) for EBD Stopping threshold.

## File: docs/api_endpoints_and_backend_schema.md
````markdown
  1: # IRIS AI — API Endpoints & Backend Data Structure Specification
  2: 
  3: > **Location:** `docs/api_endpoints_and_backend_schema.md`  
  4: > **System:** IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI): Automatic Block Planning & Corridor Optimization  
  5: > **Problem Statement:** SIH 26027 — *"AI-Powered Automatic Block Planning to Maximize Asset Availability for Train Operations on Indian Railways"*  
  6: > **Document Version:** 3.1.0 (Grounded Multi-Horizon Core & Fully Decoupled Policy Specification)
  7: 
  8: ---
  9: 
 10: ## 🌐 1. API Endpoints Specification
 11: 
 12: ### 1.1 Decoupled Dynamic Ingestion & Policy Endpoints
 13: * `POST /api/v1/ingestion/:sourceSystem/events`
 14:   * **Purpose:** Unified ingestion endpoint supporting pluggable adapters (`TMS`, `SMMS`, `TDMS`, `COA`, `IOT`). Stores unstructured data in `rawPayload` for dynamic field transformation.
 15:   * **Request Payload:** `BaseIngestionPayload`
 16:   * **Response:** `{ success: true, ingestedCount: 14, normalizedSection: "CSMT-KYN", quarantineCount: 0 }`
 17: * `GET /api/v1/config/policy/:divisionId`
 18:   * **Purpose:** Retrieves active divisional policy profile (safety buffers, weights, TSR parameters, horizon windows).
 19:   * **Response:** `DivisionalPolicyProfile`
 20: * `PUT /api/v1/config/policy/:divisionId`
 21:   * **Purpose:** Dynamically updates divisional policy configuration without requiring code deployment or solver restarts.
 22: * `GET /api/v1/sync/events`
 23:   * **Purpose:** State catch-up replay endpoint for disconnected UI clients (`?since_seq=N&section_id=SEC-01`).
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: ### 1.2 ML Urgency Triage & Priority Scoring Endpoints
 28: * `GET /api/v1/triage/demands`
 29:   * **Purpose:** Retrieves all pending maintenance demands across Civil, Electrical, and Signal directorates, ranked by calculated urgency score.
 30:   * **Query Params:** `sectionId=SEC-KYN-01&urgency=ALL&horizon=TACTICAL_24H`
 31:   * **Response:** `Array<MaintenanceDemandRecord>`
 32: * `POST /api/v1/triage/score`
 33:   * **Purpose:** Dynamically re-evaluates urgency score when new flaw parameters or traffic delays are detected.
 34:   * **Request Payload:** `UrgencyScoringRequest`
 35:   * **Response:** `UrgencyScoringResult` (Urgency Tier: `P1_CRITICAL` | `P2_SCHEDULED` | `P3_ROUTINE`, calculated score 0.0–1.0).
 36: 
 37: ---
 38: 
 39: ### 1.3 Joint Shadow-Block Optimizer Endpoints
 40: * `POST /api/v1/optimizer/solve-corridor`
 41:   * **Purpose:** Triggers the Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solver to generate an optimized block plan bundling co-located maintenance into traffic gaps.
 42:   * **Request Body:**
 43:     ```json
 44:     {
 45:       "corridorSectionId": "CSMT-KYN-UP",
 46:       "horizon": "TACTICAL_24H",
 47:       "targetDate": "2026-09-06",
 48:       "maxAllowedFreightDelayMinutes": 30,
 49:       "allowNightLullOnly": true
 50:     }
 51:     ```
 52:   * **Response Body:** `BlockPlanResolution`
 53:     * Array of bundled joint block windows.
 54:     * Corridor downtime saved percentage (e.g. `38.4%`).
 55:     * Train delay impact summary (`zeroPassengerDelays: true`).
 56:     * Kavach TSR speed restrictions generated.
 57: * `GET /api/v1/optimizer/schedules/active`
 58:   * **Purpose:** Returns the current corridor schedule for the Time-Distance String Chart / Gantt UI.
 59:   * **Query Params:** `horizon=TACTICAL_24H`
 60:   * **Response:** `CorridorScheduleView`
 61: 
 62: ---
 63: 
 64: ### 1.4 e-BDMS Sanction & Controller Workflow Endpoints
 65: * `POST /api/v1/blocks/:blockId/sanction`
 66:   * **Purpose:** Section Controller one-click sanction of an AI-recommended joint maintenance block.
 67:   * **Request Body:**
 68:     ```json
 69:     {
 70:       "operatorId": "CTRL-MUM-402",
 71:       "approvalMode": "ADVISORY",
 72:       "sanctionedSlot": {
 73:         "startTime": "2026-09-06T01:30:00Z",
 74:         "endTime": "2026-09-06T04:45:00Z"
 75:       },
 76:       "enforceKavachTsr": true
 77:     }
 78:     ```
 79:   * **Response:** `BlockSanctionResponse` (Block ID, Sanction Status `SANCTIONED`, Kavach TSR Broadcast ID, SHA-256 Audit Seal).
 80: * `POST /api/v1/blocks/:blockId/reject`
 81:   * **Purpose:** Controller rejects a proposed block with operational justification, prompting the solver to find an alternative window.
 82:   * **Request Body:** `{ "reason": "Late running express train 12138", "alternativePreference": "AFTER_0300" }`
 83: 
 84: ---
 85: 
 86: ### 1.5 Safety, Kavach TSR & Interlocking Endpoints
 87: * `GET /api/v1/safety/kavach-tsr/active`
 88:   * **Purpose:** Streams all active Temporary Speed Restrictions broadcast to locomotive cab units.
 89:   * **Response:** `Array<KavachTsrPacket>`
 90: * `GET /api/v1/safety/interlocking-status/:sectionId`
 91:   * **Purpose:** Returns live track circuit occupancy and signal lockout aspects for circuits `TC-01` through `TC-06`.
 92:   * **Response:** `TrackInterlockingState`
 93: 
 94: ---
 95: 
 96: ## 📦 2. Core Backend Data Schemas (TypeScript & Pydantic)
 97: 
 98: ### 2.1 Unified Maintenance Demand Model
 99: ```typescript
100: export type DepartmentCode = 'TMS_CIVIL' | 'TDMS_ELECTRICAL' | 'SMMS_SIGNAL';
101: export type UrgencyTier = 'P1_CRITICAL' | 'P2_SCHEDULED' | 'P3_ROUTINE';
102: 
103: export interface MaintenanceDemandRecord {
104:   demandId: string;
105:   department: DepartmentCode;
106:   assetType: 'RAIL_TRACK' | 'OHE_CATENARY' | 'POINT_MACHINE' | 'TRACK_CIRCUIT';
107:   sectionId: string;
108:   chainageStartKm: number; // e.g. 108.4
109:   chainageEndKm: number;   // e.g. 112.2
110:   trackCircuitId: string;  // e.g. "TC-03"
111:   urgencyTier: UrgencyTier;
112:   urgencyScore: number;    // 0.00 - 1.00
113:   estimatedDurationMinutes: number;
114:   requiredAssets: string[]; // e.g. ["CSM_TAMPER_98", "TOWER_WAGON_04"]
115:   canShadowBlock: boolean;
116:   status: 'PENDING_TRIAGE' | 'SLOTTED' | 'SANCTIONED' | 'COMPLETED';
117: }
118: ```
119: 
120: ### 2.2 Train Schedule & Path Slot Model
121: ```typescript
122: export interface TrainScheduleSlot {
123:   trainNumber: string;
124:   trainName: string;
125:   trainType: 'PREMIUM_PASSENGER' | 'EXPRESS_PASSENGER' | 'SUBURBAN' | 'FREIGHT';
126:   sectionId: string;
127:   entryTime: string;
128:   exitTime: string;
129:   isDelayTolerant: boolean;
130:   maxAllowableDelayMinutes: number;
131:   priorityRank: number; // 1 (highest) to 5
132: }
133: ```
134: 
135: ### 2.3 Joint Shadow-Block Resolution Model
136: ```typescript
137: export interface JointBlockPlan {
138:   blockId: string;
139:   sectionId: string;
140:   trackCircuitIds: string[]; // ["TC-03", "TC-04"]
141:   startTime: string;
142:   endTime: string;
143:   durationMinutes: number;
144:   bundledDemands: MaintenanceDemandRecord[];
145:   coLocatedSavingsMinutes: number;
146:   trafficLullIdentified: string; // e.g. "01:30 - 04:45 IST Night Window"
147:   passengerCancellations: number; // Strictly 0

150:     tsrSpeedKmh: number; // e.g. 30 km/h
151:     affectedSections: string[];
152:     broadcastStatus: 'ARMED' | 'BROADCASTING' | 'CLEARED';
153:   };
154:   sanctionStatus: 'RECOMMENDED' | 'SANCTIONED' | 'REJECTED';
155: }
156: ```
157: 
158: ### 2.4 Explainable Decision Dossier Model
159: ```typescript
160: export interface ExplainableDecisionDossier {

162:   corridorSection: string;

164:   sanctionedBy: string;

167:     {
168:       step: 1;
169:       title: "Multi-Source Data Ingestion";

171:     },
172:     {
173:       step: 2;
174:       title: "Traffic Conflict & Headway Analysis";
175:       detail: "Avoided 14:00 freight path bottleneck. Identified natural 3h 15m night traffic lull.";
176:     },
177:     {
178:       step: 3;
179:       title: "Joint Shadow-Block Bundling";
180:       detail: "Bundled OHE catenary wash with civil track tamping under single 210-min window, saving 85 mins of downtime.";
181:     },
182:     {

184:       title: "Safety Dissemination & Sanction Output";

## File: docs/architecture_walkthrough.md
````markdown
  1: # IRIS AI — Architecture & Technical Walkthrough
  2: 
  3: > **System Name:** IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI): Automatic Block Planning & Corridor Optimization  
  4: > **Problem Statement:** SIH 26027 — *"AI-Powered Automatic Block Planning to Maximize Asset Availability for Train Operations on Indian Railways"*  
  5: > **Document Version:** 2.0.0 (SIH 26027 Refactored Architecture)  
  6: > **Target Framework:** Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, FastAPI / Python MILP (OR-Tools)
  7: 
  8: ---
  9: 
 10: ## 🏗️ 1. High-Level System Architecture
 11: 
 12: IRIS AI utilizes an **Event-Driven Service-Oriented Architecture** connected to an **Optimization Core** and **Real-Time Controller Cockpit**:
 13: 
 14: ```text
 15: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 16: │                                   CLIENT LAYER (NEXT.JS 16 / REACT 19)                           │
 17: │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
 18: │  │ Mintlify Light-Blue Design System (#F0F6FC Base, #FFFFFF Cards, #2B7FFF Accent, 4px Radii)│  │
 19: │  │                                                                                            │  │
 20: │  │  • TAB 1: Automatic Corridor Block Planner (Time-Distance String Chart / Gantt Visualizer) │  │
 21: │  │  • TAB 2: Section Interlocking & Circuit Map (Circuits TC-01..06, Signals S-12..16)         │  │
 22: │  │  • TAB 3: Vision Defect Feeds (TMS Track Cam, TDMS Pantograph Cam, SMMS Axle Cam)         │  │
 23: │  │  • TAB 4: Auditor Workspace & BDMS Decision Dossier (4-Step Timeline & RDSO Form 14B)      │  │
 24: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
 25: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 26:                                                   │ REST / SSE / WebSockets
 27: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 28: │                                   BACKEND APPLICATION SERVICES (FASTAPI)                         │
 29: │  ┌──────────────────────────┐   ┌───────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────────┐  │
 30: │  │ API Gateway & Router     │   │ Real-Time WebSocket Hub   │   │ e-BDMS Sanction Coordinator │  │
 31: │  │ (Demands / Timetables)   │   │ (Train Pos / TSR Stream)  │   │ (Advisory vs Autonomous)    │  │
 32: │  └────────────┬─────────────┘   └─────────────┬─────────────┘   └──────────────┬──────────────┘  │
 33: └───────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┘
 34:                 │                               │                                │
 35: ┌───────────────▼───────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────┐
 36: │                           AI & MATHEMATICAL OPTIMIZATION CORE                                     │
 37: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
 38: │  │ 1. MULTI-SOURCE INGESTION ADAPTER (TMS Flaws, SMMS Signals, TDMS OHE, COA Timetables)       │  │
 39: │  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
 40: │  │ 2. ML URGENCY TRIAGE CLASSIFIER (Dynamic Priority Scoring: P1 Critical / P2 / P3)           │  │
 41: │  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
 42: │  │ 3. JOINT SHADOW-BLOCK OPTIMIZER (Google OR-Tools MILP Solver & Co-Location Clustering)      │  │
 43: │  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
 44: │  │ 4. KAVACH TSR GENERATOR & AUDIT LOGGER (RDSO Chapter 15 Speed Limits & SHA-256 Dossier)     │  │
 45: │  └────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
 46: └───────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 47:                                                 │
 48: ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 49: │                                  RAILWAY FIELD & INTERLOCKING LAYER                               │
 50: │  ┌──────────────────────────┐   ┌───────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────────┐  │
 51: │  │ Kavach Loco TCAS Units   │   │ Electronic Interlocking   │   │ Trackside Balises & Relays  │  │
 52: │  │ (Digital TSR Broadcast)  │   │ (Signal S-12/14 Clamping) │   │ (Circuits TC-01 to TC-06)   │  │
 53: │  └──────────────────────────┘   └───────────────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────────┘  │
 54: └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 55: ```
 56: 
 57: ---
 58: 
 59: ## 🔄 2. End-to-End Data Flow & Optimization Pipeline
 60: 
 61: The complete lifecycle of a corridor block plan follows a 5-stage sequential pipeline:
 62: 
 63: ```mermaid
 64: sequenceDiagram
 65:     autonumber
 66:     participant CRIS as CRIS Portals (TMS/SMMS/TDMS/COA)
 67:     participant Ingest as Ingestion & Normalizer Adapter
 68:     participant Solver as Joint Shadow-Block Optimizer (MILP)
 69:     participant Cockpit as Section Controller Cockpit
 70:     participant Kavach as Kavach TCAS & Interlocking Relays
 71:     participant Audit as Explainable Audit Dossier
 72: 
 73:     CRIS->>Ingest: Transmit defect logs, overdue tasks & COA train timetables
 74:     Ingest->>Ingest: Normalize spatial chainage (KM) into Track Circuits (TC-01..06)
 75:     Ingest->>Solver: Stream unified demands + train schedule slots
 76:     Solver->>Solver: Search natural traffic lulls & bundle co-located shadow blocks
 77:     Solver->>Cockpit: Render proposed block schedule on Time-Distance String Chart
 78:     Cockpit->>Cockpit: Controller reviews co-located savings (e.g. 3 blocks bundled into 1)
 79:     Cockpit->>Solver: Click [SANCTION BLOCK]
 80:     Solver->>Kavach: Broadcast Temporary Speed Restrictions (TSR 30 km/h) to locos
 81:     Solver->>Kavach: Clamp interlocking signals (Red aspect S-12)
 82:     Solver->>Audit: Generate immutable 4-step decision log with SHA-256 seal
 83: ```
 84: 
 85: ---
 86: 
 87: ## 💻 3. Frontend Architecture (Next.js 16 + React 19)
 88: 
 89: ### 3.1 Design System Tokens & Mintlify Discipline
 90: The frontend adheres to the **Light-Blue Mintlify Theme**:
 91: * **Surface 0 (Canvas Base):** `#F0F6FC` (atmospheric soft ice-blue canvas)
 92: * **Surface 1 (Cards/Panels):** `#FFFFFF` with 1px border `#D0DFEE`
 93: * **Surface 2 (Elevated Tabs/Inputs):** `#E6F0FA`
 94: * **Primary Accent:** `#2B7FFF` (Signal Blue)
 95: * **Atmospheric Accent:** `#426188` (Twilight Blue)
 96: * **Typography Primary:** `#0F172A` (Ink Slate)
 97: * **Geometry:** `4px` button/input radius, `16px` card radius, `24px` container radius (**Strictly ZERO pill buttons**).
 98: * **Font Family:** `Inter` for UI typography paired with `JetBrains Mono` for tabular monospaced numbers (KM markers, signal IDs, timestamps, and speeds).
 99: 
100: ### 3.2 Key UI Components
101: 
102: 1. **Corridor Time-Distance String Chart (`CorridorStringChart.tsx`):**
103:    * High-performance SVG visualization rendering train time-distance trajectories (slanted paths) alongside scheduled maintenance block windows (colored shaded boxes).
104:    * Displays natural white corridors and highlights multi-department co-location savings.
105: 2. **Department Demand Triage Queue (`IncidentQueue.tsx`):**
106:    * Filterable list of pending work orders across Civil (TMS), Electrical (TDMS), and Signal (SMMS).
107:    * Displays urgency badges (P1 Critical, P2 Scheduled, P3 Routine), estimated duration, required machine assets (CSM Tamper, Tower Wagon), and joint bundling suggestions.
108: 3. **KPI Strip (`KpiStrip.tsx`):**
109:    * 6 real-time operational cards:
110:      * **Corridor Downtime Saved:** `38.4%` (via shadow blocking).
111:      * **Track Availability Index:** `96.2%`.
112:      * **Active Corridor Blocks:** `03 Active`.
113:      * **Pending Demands:** `08 In Queue`.
114:      * **White Corridor Gap:** `3h 15m`.
115:      * **Active Kavach TSRs:** `02 Enforced`.
116: 4. **Track Interlocking & Circuit Map (`InterlockingMap.tsx`):**
117:    * Top-down circuit view (`TC-01` to `TC-06`) showing live train occupancy, signal aspects (`S-12`, `S-14`, `S-16`), turnout positions (`SW-04`), and maintenance block lockout boundaries.
118: 5. **Decision Dossier Drawer Modal (`DecisionLogModal.tsx`):**
119:    * Chronological 4-step explainable record justifying why a block was sanctioned at a specific time:
120:      1. *Ingestion:* Aggregated 3 TMS defects, 1 TDMS power cut, and COA timetables.
121:      2. *Conflict Analysis:* Avoided 14:00 peak freight corridor.
122:      3. *Shadow Optimization:* Slotted into 02:15 AM lull, bundling catenary wash with track tamping.
123:      4. *Safety & Output:* Zero passenger delays, 85 mins saved, Kavach TSR 30 km/h broadcast.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## 🧮 4. Mathematical Optimization Formulation (MILP)
128: 
129: The core optimization engine is formulated as a **Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP)** solved via Google OR-Tools:
130: 
131: ### 4.1 Decision Variables
132: * $x_{i,t} \in \{0, 1\}$: Binary variable indicating if maintenance demand $i$ is executed starting at time slot $t$.
133: * $y_{s,t} \in \{0, 1\}$: Binary variable indicating if track section $s$ is blocked at time $t$.
134: * $d_j \ge 0$: Continuous variable representing the delay incurred by train $j$.
135: 
136: ### 4.2 Objective Function
137: $$\min \quad \sum_{s,t} C_{\text{block}} \cdot y_{s,t} + \sum_j C_{\text{delay}, j} \cdot d_j + \sum_i P_{\text{defer}, i} \cdot (1 - \sum_t x_{i,t})$$
138: Where:
139: * $C_{\text{block}}$ is the hourly cost of corridor track closure.
140: * $C_{\text{delay}, j}$ is the penalty cost per minute of delay for train $j$ (higher penalty for passenger vs freight).
141: * $P_{\text{defer}, i}$ is the penalty for deferring maintenance task $i$ past its deadline.
142: 
143: ### 4.3 Key Constraints
144: 1. **Multi-Department Shadow Co-Location:** If demand $i_1$ (TDMS) and demand $i_2$ (TMS) share section $s$, they share the same track closure variable:
145:    $$x_{i_1, t} \le y_{s, t} \quad \text{and} \quad x_{i_2, t} \le y_{s, t}$$
146: 2. **Headway Separation:** Minimum safety buffer $H_{\text{min}} = 15\text{ min}$ between the last cleared train and block start.
147: 3. **Zero Passenger Delay:** For all scheduled passenger trains $j \in \mathcal{P}$:
148:    $$d_j = 0$$
149: 
150: ---
151: 
152: ## 🛡️ 5. RDSO Safety & Kavach Integration
153: 
154: * **Kavach TCAS Dissemination:** Conforms to RDSO Specification `RDSO/SPN/196/2020`. Once a block is sanctioned, temporary speed restrictions (TSR) are wirelessly injected into locomotive cab onboard units.
155: * **Interlocking Integrity:** Electronic interlocking routes over the maintenance block section are clamped to prevent accidental green aspect clearing.
156: * **Compliance Archival:** Every sanctioned block generates an immutable SHA-256 signed audit dossier ready for RDSO Section 14B inspections.
````

## File: docs/MASTER_RESEARCH_AND_SYSTEM_WRITEUP.md
````markdown
  1: # IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI): Comprehensive System Architecture & Research Dossier
  2: 
  3: > **Problem Statement ID:** Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 26027  
  4: > **Official Title:** AI-Powered Automatic Block Planning to Maximize Asset Availability for Train Operations on Indian Railways  
  5: > **Target System:** Auto-BDMS (Automated Block & Disconnection Management System) & Joint Corridor Time-Distance Optimizer  
  6: > **Governing Standards:** IRPWM 2020, ACTM Vol II, IRSEM 2021, G&SR Chapter 15, RDSO TCAS Specification RDSO/SPN/196/2020 (Kavach Ver 4.0), and Google OR-Tools CP-SAT.
  7: 
  8: ---
  9: 
 10: ## I. Title & System Identity
 11: 
 12: * **Project Title:** IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI) — AI-Powered Automatic Block Planning and Corridor Optimization System.
 13: * **Target Classification:** Auto-BDMS (Automated Block & Disconnection Management System) with Integrated Kavach ATP Safety Swarm.
 14: * **Problem Scope:** Transforming manual, fragmented, inter-departmental railway maintenance requests into automated, constraint-optimized Joint Shadow Blocks across high-density corridors.
 15: * **Regulatory Compliance:** Engineered in strict accordance with the Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual (**IRPWM 2020**), AC Traction Manual (**ACTM Vol II**), Indian Railways Signal Engineering Manual (**IRSEM 2021**), General and Subsidiary Rules (**G&SR Chapter 15**), and RDSO TCAS Specifications (**RDSO/SPN/196/2020**).
 16: 
 17: ---
 18: 
 19: ## II. Description & The Operational Problem
 20: 
 21: ### 1. The Real-World Railway Context
 22: Indian Railways is the fourth-largest rail network in the world, operating more than 13,000 passenger trains and 8,000 freight rakes every day across 68,000 route kilometers. To keep trains running safely at speeds up to 130–160 km/h, tracks, electrical wires, and signals must be inspected and repaired continuously.
 23: 
 24: Three independent engineering directorates maintain these assets:
 25: 1. **Civil Engineering (Permanent Way / P-Way):** Maintains physical rails, concrete sleepers, crushed-stone ballast beds, points, crossings, and bridges. Uses heavy on-track machinery such as Continuous Action Tampers (CSM, Duomatic), Dynamic Track Stabilizers (DTS), and Ballast Cleaning Machines (BCM). Track flaws are logged in the **Track Management System (TMS)** per *IRPWM 2020*.
 26: 2. **Electrical / Traction Distribution (TRD):** Maintains 25,000-volt AC Overhead Equipment (OHE), catenary and contact wires, traction substations, and neutral sections. Line crews use motorized Tower Wagons to inspect contact wire wear and wash insulators. Maintenance records are tracked in the **Traction Distribution Management System (TDMS)** per *ACTM Vol II*.
 27: 3. **Signal & Telecommunication (S&T):** Maintains electronic interlocking (EI) systems, motorized point machines, track circuits (DC and Audio Frequency), axle counters, and trackside Kavach RFID balises. Defect logs and statutory disconnection notices are processed in the **Signalling Maintenance & Management System (SMMS)** per *IRSEM 2021*.
 28: 4. **Traffic / Operating Directorate:** Section Controllers and Station Masters manage train dispatching, timetables, and train precedence (Rajdhani and Vande Bharat > Mail/Express > Freight) via the **Control Office Application (COA)**.
 29: 
 30: ### 2. The Core Bottleneck: Siloed Requisitions & Corridor Fragmentation
 31: To perform maintenance safely on a track, engineers must secure a **"Block"** (a temporary suspension of train traffic or a 25kV electrical power shutdown). In the existing operational workflow, each department submits standalone requests through legacy portals (e-BDMS) or paper memos without cross-departmental coordination:
 32: 
 33: * **Monday:** Civil Engineering secures a 3-hour block on Track Section A-B for track tamping.
 34: * **Wednesday:** Electrical TRD secures a 2.5-hour power cutoff on the *exact same section* to replace worn contact wire.
 35: * **Friday:** S&T secures a 2-hour block on the *exact same section* to overhaul point machines.
 36: 
 37: **The Failure Mode:** The railway corridor is shut down **three separate times in a single week**, causing 7.5 hours of accumulated traffic disruption. Section Controllers in the Divisional Control Office, under immense pressure to prevent train delays, frequently reject or truncate maintenance requests. This leads to **deferred maintenance**, increased risks of rail fractures or OHE breakdowns, and emergency **Temporary Speed Restrictions (TSRs)** that permanently slow down train operations.
 38: 
 39: ```mermaid
 40: gantt
 41:     title Traditional Siloed Requisitions (7.5 Hours Total Disruption)
 42:     dateFormat  X
 43:     axisFormat %d
 44:     section Civil P-Way
 45:     Track Tamping (TMS) :active, 0, 3
 46:     section Electrical TRD
 47:     OHE Maintenance (TDMS) :crit, 5, 8
 48:     section S&T
 49:     Point Machine Overhaul (SMMS) :done, 10, 12
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ### 3. The Solution: Automated Joint Shadow Blocking
 53: IRIS AI (Intelligent Railway Inspection and Restoration AI) introduces an automated mathematical solver that eliminates siloed planning. When an electrical power cutoff is approved for Section A-B, the solver checks TMS and SMMS for pending work on the same spatial track section. It automatically bundles all three maintenance tasks into a single **3.5-hour Joint Shadow Block** during natural nocturnal traffic lulls (01:30 AM to 05:00 AM).
 54: 
 55: Civil track gangs and S&T technicians work safely underneath the de-energized electrical catenary wire simultaneously. The result is a **35% to 50% reduction in corridor downtime**, zero passenger train cancellations, and complete regulatory compliance.
 56: 
 57: ```mermaid
 58: gantt
 59:     title IRIS AI Joint Shadow Block (3.5 Hours Single Window)
 60:     dateFormat X
 61:     axisFormat %d
 62:     section Primary Constraint

 66:     section Co-Located Shadow 2
 67:     S&T Point Overhaul (SMMS) :done, 1, 3
 68: ```

 72: ## III. Major Components & System Architecture
 73: 
 74: IRIS AI executes a continuous **4-Step Operational Loop**:
 75: 
 76: ```mermaid
 77: graph TD
 78:     subgraph Step1 [Step 1: Multi-System Data Ingestion]
 79:         TMS["TMS (Civil P-Way)<br/>• USFD Defects (IMR/OBS/REM)<br/>• Track Geometry Index (TGI)"]
 80:         TDMS["TDMS (Electrical TRD)<br/>• 25kV OHE Contact Wire Wear<br/>• Insulator Wash Cycles"]
 81:         SMMS["SMMS (S&T)<br/>• Point Machine Diagnostics<br/>• Form S&T/T-351 Notices"]
 82:         COA["COA (Traffic / Operating)<br/>• Live Train GPS & Delays<br/>• Freight Path Forecasts"]
 83:     end
 84: 
 85:     TMS --> Adapter["Unified Spatial Ingestion Adapter<br/>(Kilometer Chainage → Track Circuit IDs)"]
 86:     TDMS --> Adapter
 87:     SMMS --> Adapter
 88:     COA --> Adapter
 89: 
 90:     Adapter --> Step2["Step 2: ML Urgency Triage & Priority Scoring<br/>(P1 Critical / P2 Periodic / P3 Routine)"]
 91: 
 92:     Step2 --> Step3["Step 3: Joint Shadow-Block MILP Optimizer<br/>(Google OR-Tools CP-SAT Disjunctive Solver)"]
 93: 
 94:     Step3 --> Step4["Step 4: Safety & Sanction Dispatch Gate"]
 95: 
 96:     subgraph Actuations [Step 4 Dispatch Actions]
 97:         Step4 --> KAVACH["Kavach TCAS Wireless TSR Injection (30 km/h)"]
 98:         Step4 --> LOCK["Electronic Interlocking Lockout (Form S&T/T-351)"]
 99:         Step4 --> CAUTION["Digital Caution Order Broadcast (Form T/409)"]
100:         Step4 --> AUDIT["Immutable SHA-256 Decision Dossier"]
101:     end
102: ```
103: 
104: ### 1. Multi-System Ingestion & Spatial Chainage Adapter
105: * **The Problem:** Legacy railway databases record maintenance locations using physical kilometer posts (e.g., `KM 108/4 to 112/2`). Electrical OHE records reference catenary mast numbers (e.g., `Mast 108/12`), and S&T systems reference point machine numbers (e.g., `Point 104A`).
106: * **The Implementation:** The Unified Ingestion Adapter maps continuous physical linear chainages into discrete, logical **Track Circuit IDs** (e.g., `TC-01` through `TC-06`). This ensures all directorates and algorithms operate on the exact same physical segment of track.
107: 
108: ### 2. ML Urgency Triage & Priority Scoring
109: Every defect and maintenance request is evaluated by a composite mathematical priority scoring algorithm:
110: $$\text{Urgency Score} = 0.40 \cdot \text{Defect Severity} + 0.35 \cdot \text{Days Overdue} + 0.25 \cdot \text{Corridor Traffic Density}$$
111: 
112: Demands are classified into three actionable tiers:
113: * **P1 Critical (Score 80–100):** Immediate safety risks such as rail fractures (IMR flaws per *IRPWM 2020*), acute catenary wire sag ($< 8.25\text{ mm}$ residual thickness), or track circuit drops. Automatically slotted into the next 24-hour tactical night lull or protected with emergency caution orders.
114: * **P2 Periodic (Score 50–79):** Machine-bound periodic maintenance such as track tamping cycles (TGI score $< 36$) and point motor overhauls. Bundled into 7-day rolling corridor maintenance windows.
115: * **P3 Routine (Score 0–49):** Preventive tasks such as drain clearing, cess repairs, and insulator washing. Slotted into 30-day cyclical maintenance overhauls.
116: 
117: ### 3. Joint Shadow-Block Optimizer Engine (Google OR-Tools CP-SAT)
118: The mathematical core is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) utilizing constraint programming interval variables:
119: * **Objective Function:** Minimize total corridor downtime, train delay penalties, and deferred maintenance risks while maximizing shadow block synergy:
120:   $$\min Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in B} \text{DowntimeCost}(i) + \beta \sum_{j \in \text{Trains}} \text{DelayCost}(j) + \delta \sum_{k \in \text{Defects}} \text{Risk}(k) - \gamma \sum_{m \in \text{Shadow}} \text{Synergy}(m)$$
121: * **Hard Safety Constraints:**
122:   1. *Earthing Buffer:* A mandatory $\ge 10\text{ minute}$ electrical discharge earthing window ($\Delta_{\text{earth}}$) before track work begins, and a $10\text{ minute}$ restoration buffer ($\Delta_{\text{restore}}$) before re-energization.
123:   2. *Passenger Clearance Headway:* A mandatory $\ge 15\text{ minute}$ safety clearance window ($\Delta_{\text{clear}}$) between block termination and high-priority passenger train arrival.
124:   3. *Machine Contiguity:* Heavy track tampers (CSM) and Tower Wagons cannot teleport; transit times between stations are enforced mathematically.
125: 
126: ### 4. Safety Dispatch, Kavach TCAS & Regulatory Lockouts
127: When the Section Controller clicks `[SANCTION BLOCK]`:
128: * **Kavach TCAS ATP Wireless Injection:** The Temporary Speed Restriction Management System (TSRMS) transmits digital speed caps ($30\text{ km/h}$) directly to approaching locomotive cab units over UHF/LTE radio per *RDSO/SPN/196/2020*.
129: * **Interlocking Lockout (Form S&T/T-351):** The Station Master's electronic interlocking panel is digitally clamped to hold entrance signals at Red.
130: * **Caution Orders (Form T/409):** Digital caution notices are issued automatically to loco pilots and train managers.
131: * **Auditor Compliance Dossier:** An immutable 4-step decision record is sealed with a SHA-256 cryptographic hash, complying with *RDSO Chapter 15* safety regulations.
132:

148: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
149: | **Horizon 1: 24-Hour Tactical** | 24 Hours | 1 Hour | Night-lull slotting ($01:30\text{--}04:30\text{ AM}$), emergent P1 USFD IMR flaw patching, dynamic freight pathing, Kavach wireless TSR broadcast. | Real-time conflict resolution, 15-min train clearance buffers. |
150: | **Horizon 2: 7-Day Operational** | 7 Days | 24 Hours | Multi-department joint shadow block bundling, heavy machine (CSM tamper, Tower Wagon) route planning, passenger diversions. | CP-SAT disjunctive scheduling, CRIS Rolling Block System. |
151: | **Horizon 3: 26-Week Strategic** | 26 Weeks | 1 Week | High-capacity machine routing (BCM ballast cleaners), Track Geometry Index (TGI) recovery, seasonal fog/monsoon prep. | Stochastic degradation tracking, Indian Railways GR 15.02 (Rolling Block Programme). |

221: $$D_{\text{stop}} = \frac{V^2}{2g(\mu + G)} + V \cdot t_{\text{reaction}}$$
222: 
223: | Weather Condition | Friction Coefficient ($\mu$) | Stopping Distance @ 130 km/h | Stopping Distance @ 100 km/h | Safety Behavior |
224: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
225: | **Dry Standard Track** | $\mu = 0.134$ | **703 meters** | **442 meters** | Standard RDSO braking curve. |
226: | **Monsoon Rain / Wet Rail** | $\mu = 0.095$ | **965 meters (+37%)** | **607 meters** | Expands safety horizon; earlier braking. |
227: | **Winter Fog / Moisture** | $\mu = 0.115$ | **808 meters (+15%)** | **508 meters** | Activates cab infrared enhancement. |
228: | **Night Vision (IR)** | $\mu = 0.134$ | **703 meters** | **442 meters** | Active thermal sensor fusion. |

247: 4. **RDSO TCAS Specification RDSO/SPN/196/2020 (Kavach Ver 4.0):** Standard for Automatic Train Protection (ATP), Stationary Kavach, Radio Block Centers (RBC), and Temporary Speed Restriction Management System (TSRMS).
248: 5. **Indian Railways General & Subsidiary Rules (G&SR Chapter 15):** Protocols for traffic block sanctions, safety clearance buffers ($\Delta_{\text{clear}} \ge 15\text{ min}$), and **Form T/409** Caution Orders.

 29: # 1. The Real-World Context & Problem Statement Breakdown
 30: 
 31: ### 1.1 The Operational Challenge
 32: Indian Railways runs over **13,000 passenger trains** and **8,000+ freight rakes** daily over **68,000+ route kilometers**. To maintain track integrity, high-voltage traction, and advanced signaling, three distinct engineering directorates constantly require track access ("Blocks" or "Disconnections"):
 33: - **Civil Engineering (P-Way):** Track rails, sleepers, ballast cleaning, USFD ultrasonic rail flaw repairs, tamping.
 34: - **Electrical (TRD):** 25kV Overhead Equipment (OHE) catenary wires, contact wire wear, insulator washing, power substations.
 35: - **Signal & Telecom (S&T):** Point machines, track circuits, axle counters, electronic interlocking, Kavach balises.
 36: 
 37: ### 1.2 The Failure of the Current Manual Process
 38: Currently, each department submits separate paper or standalone digital requests through the **Block Demand Management System (BDMS)**:
 39: 1. **Departmental Silos:** Civil takes a 3-hour block on Monday. Electrical takes a 2.5-hour block on Wednesday on the *exact same section*. S&T takes a 2-hour block on Friday. The result: the corridor is shut down **three separate times in one week**, multiplying train delays and killing freight throughput.
 40: 2. **Controller Overload in COA:** The Section Controller in the Divisional Control Office uses **COA (Control Office Application)**. Under heavy pressure to maintain punctuality, controllers often reject maintenance blocks or cut them short. This leads to **deferred maintenance**, higher accident risks, and emergency **Temporary Speed Restrictions (TSRs)** that permanently slow down trains.
 41: 3. **Lack of Integrated Multi-Horizon Planning:** Controllers only look 2 to 4 hours ahead. They lack tools to forecast train paths over **24 hours (Tactical)**, **7 days (Operational)**, or **26 weeks (Strategic Rolling Block Programme)** using a dynamic Rolling Horizon Framework.

 44: 
 45: # 2. Domain Knowledge & Railway Glossary (The 4 Siloed Systems)
 46: 
 47: To explain this clearly, you must master the 4 core CRIS / Railway systems:
 48: 
 49: | System | Directorate / Dept | What It Manages | Data Ingested by IRIS AI |
 50: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 51: | **TMS** *(Track Management System)* | Civil / Permanent Way (P-Way) | Track flaws, Ultrasonic Rail Flaw Detection (USFD), Track Geometry Index (TGI), track tamping machines (CSM, BCM). | Flaw coordinates, Chainage KM (`KM 108/4 - 112/2`), track wear severity, urgent tamping needs. |
 52: | **TDMS** *(Traction Distribution Mgmt System)* | Electrical / Traction (TRD) | 25kV OHE catenary & contact wires, insulator cleanliness, Tower Wagons, traction substations (TSS). | Power block requisitions (OHE de-energization), insulator wash schedules, catenary defect locations. |
 53: | **SMMS** *(Signalling Maintenance System)* | Signal & Telecom (S&T) | Point machines, track circuits, axle counters, electronic interlocking (EI), Kavach RFID tags. | Disconnection requisitions, signal overhaul schedules, point machine replacement alerts. |
 54: | **COA** *(Control Office Application)* | Traffic / Operations (DOM / Section Controller) | Live train movements, scheduled passenger timetables, goods/freight forecasts, section capacity. | Train schedules, headway gaps, train priorities (Rajdhani > Express > Goods), live delay feeds. |
 55: 
 56: ### Key Railway Operational Terms
 57: - **Traffic Block:** Complete suspension of train movement on a specific track section to allow heavy track machines (e.g., CSM tamper) or civil works.
 58: - **Power Block:** De-energization (cutting off the 25kV power) of the overhead catenary wire to allow electrical linemen and Tower Wagons to work safely.
 59: - **Disconnection:** Taking a signal, point machine, or track circuit offline for maintenance, requiring manual interlocking safety protocols.
 60: - **Shadow Block (The Secret Weapon):** An integrated multi-departmental block where Civil, Electrical, and Signal teams execute their maintenance **simultaneously in the same spatial section and time slot**. (1 shutdown instead of 3).
 61: - **Kavach TCAS:** India's Indigenous Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system. When a block is active, digital speed limits (TSR) are pushed directly over UHF/LTE radio into the locomotive cab.
 62: - **Chainage (KM):** Railway distance marker (e.g., `KM 142/10` to `KM 146/4`) identifying exact track physical location.
